c.titolo_copertina: Xi, Trump e Putin al primo vertice a tre: sul tavolo pace e nucleare

slide.titolo: Giovedì a Shenzhen il primo trilaterale della storia
slide.testo: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump e Vladimir Putin si incontrano a margine del vertice Apec. È il primo colloquio di questo tipo. La Cina è stata l'ultima delle tre potenze a confermarlo, senza indicare punti precisi dell'agenda.
I leader si scambieranno opinioni in modo approfondito sulla salvaguardia della pace mondiale e sulla promozione della stabilità strategica nei rapporti tra grandi potenze.
slide.autore: Mao Ning, portavoce del ministero degli Esteri cinese

slide.testo: «Tema difficile», ha detto Trump: è dura per chiunque dire che rinuncerà alle proprie testate. Guterres, segretario generale Onu: un impegno concreto sarebbe «un grande risultato per il mondo». Secondo il Guardian, la Cina ha sempre respinto questi negoziati.

Secondo funzionari Usa citati dal Guardian, Trump non dovrebbe sollevare il tema. Trump invece ha detto che si parlerà delle guerre in Iran e Ucraina. Il Cremlino annuncia un incontro Putin-Xi il 18 novembre, anche sull'Ucraina.

slide.titolo: Trump potrebbe vedere anche Kim Jong-un
slide.testo: «Forse incontreremo anche Kim», ha detto Trump prima di partire. Ad agosto aveva detto che il leader nordcoreano possiede 57 armi nucleari «molto potenti». L'Aiea si è detta seriamente preoccupata per la produzione nucleare di Pyongyang.

slide.titolo: Gli analisti: più simboli che risultati
slide.testo: Per Ryan Hass (Brookings), il valore simbolico potrebbe durare più dei contenuti. Secondo il Wall Street Journal, Washington si è opposta alla richiesta di Pechino di un vertice rigidamente programmato, con dichiarazioni già preparate.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: Le tre maggiori potenze nucleari discutono di armi atomiche e della guerra in Iran, mentre l'Ucraina rischia di restare fuori. Sono dossier da cui dipendono la sicurezza europea e la stabilità dei mercati.

sources.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ at trilateral, says China
sources.text:
The meeting of Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen this week will cover topics of “groundbreaking significance” including “safeguarding world peace”, the Chinese foreign ministry has said.
The confirmation of Thursday’s first-of-their-kind trilateral talks, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, cements Xi’s status as a global powerbroker as he presides over events in the glittering southern tech hub of Shenzhen.
The topics up for discussion are far from clear but many – including the UN secretary general – are hoping that denuclearisation will be discussed between the world’s three largest nuclear powers.
In a call this week, China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi, and the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearisation”, the US state department said.
China was the last of the three powers to confirm the trilateral meeting was happening, and its statement stopped short of confirming specific agenda items.
“[The leaders] will exchange views in-depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance,” said the foreign ministry spokesperson, Mao Ning. “Stronger communication among China, Russia, and the United States, along with managing differences and stabilising relations, serves the interests of all three countries.”
The Kremlin said “the signficance and symbolism of this meeting are hard to overestimate”.
The UN secretary general, António Guterres, said that if the three leaders “really commit themselves to a meaningful denuclearisation, it will be a great achievement for the world”.
However, many analysts have warned to temper expectations of a major breakthrough.
Xi will “bask in the glow of China serving as the convener and agenda-setter”, wrote Brookings’ Ryan Hass in one such take. However, “symbolism may prove more enduring than the substance of this meeting”.
The three leaders would be approaching the talks with very different priorities, Xiaoyu Pu from the University of Nevada told the Guardian.
China has rebuffed previous attempts to become embroiled in nuclear arms talks with Russia and the US, which have the larger stockpiles. Trump, though, has said he wants to talk about denuclearisation, as well as the US-Israeli war in Iran. China, a top economic partner of Tehran, has sought to mediate in the conflict, and says avoiding a return to hostilities is a “top priority”.
In contrast, as feared by Kyiv, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine might not come up at all, despite Putin reportedly wanting it to.
US officials say Trump is not expected to raise the issue, and the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, said Xi showed “irritation” in a recent meeting when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.
For Xi, “much of the political benefit” will be simply in “the ability to bring Putin and Trump to the table”, Peter Alexander, the Shanghai-based managing director at Z-Ben Advisors, told CNBC.
The Wall Street Journal reported last week that the Trump administration had pushed back against Beijing’s demands that the summit be tightly scripted, with prepared statements and not much room for discussion.
Sari Arho Havrén, from the Royal United Services Institute thinktank, wrote on X: “China dislikes surprises and wants to ensure neither Trump nor Putin steals the limelight from the host. Moreover, Xi doesn’t want to be dragged into a discussion about Ukraine or anything else he is not prepared for.”

sources.title: Cremlino, 'incontro Putin e Xi prima del trilaterale, anche sull'Ucraina'
sources.text:
Putin e Xi Jinping terranno colloqui
il 18 novembre ha annunciato il consigliere presidenziale russo
Yurij Ushakov. L'incontro si svolgerà durante una colazione di
lavoro e si concentrerà su questioni di politica estera, tra cui
la situazione in Ucraina.
                                    
"Si parla di un formato molto ristretto. Le parti discuteranno
della cooperazione strategica nella regione Asia-Pacifico,
naturalmente, dell'Ucraina, della penisola coreana e così via",
ha detto Ushakov citato da Interfax.
                                    
"Il nostro presidente informerà certamente il presidente cinese
sui suoi ultimi contatti con la controparte americana, tenendo
conto anche dei risultati del recente incontro trilaterale di
Abu Dhabi", ha aggiunto il consigliere del Cremlino.
                                    
"Si può presumere che durante questo contatto bilaterale i
leader discuteranno anche del prossimo incontro, dei negoziati
trilaterali con la partecipazione del presidente degli Stati
Uniti", ha osservato Ushakov.

sources.title: Trump says he could meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in China
sources.text:
Trump is planning to discuss nuclear disarmament when he meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China this week.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he may meet with North Korean Supreme Leader Kim Jong-un in China this week.
Trump made the comments while speaking to reporters as he departed the White House to begin his trip to Asia, which will see him arrive in the Philippines early on Tuesday.
The president is then set to travel on to China, where he is scheduled to take part in trilateral talks with his Russian and Chinese counterparts Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.
"We may meet with Kim Jong-un also," Trump told the media. "So that would be good. We have the chance to accomplish a lot."
Trump is planning to discuss nuclear disarmament when he meets with Putin and Xi in Shenzhen in southeastern China this week, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
"We're going to talk about denuclearisation. Tough subject because it's very hard for any of us say we'll get rid of our nukes," Trump said on Monday. "Especially since you do have other countries."
He added that the wars in Iran and Ukraine would also come up, as well as "economics and trade."
In August, Trump talked up his relationship with Kim and said the pair would meet at some point in the year, although he gave no further details.
"The fact that I get along with him, that's a good thing not a bad thing. He has 57 very powerful nuclear weapons. Should have never allowed it to happen," the president said at the time, adding: "If I were president, I wouldn't have allowed it. But he's got them."
The director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Rafael Grossi, said in September that the reported expansion of North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material was a "cause for serious concern."
